All are buyable. Now construct JSON route.

Structure:

{
 "type":"mol",
 "smiles":"Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1",
 "children":[
   {
     "type":"reaction",
     "template_id":214705,
     "children":[
        {"type":"mol","smiles":"Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1"},
        {"type":"mol","smiles":"[intermediate A]"} // need SMILES of intermediate after amide coupling.
     ]
   }
 ]
}

Now need SMILES of intermediate A: aniline with side chain: phenyl attached to sulfonamide nitrogen after step1? Actually intermediate A is the aniline bearing the side chain but without sulfonyl group. So structure: phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) with NH2 (free) attached to that phenyl (the sulfonamide nitrogen will be attached later). The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N attached at para position of that phenyl. So SMILES: "c1ccc(Nc2ccccc2N)cc1"? Wait need correct.

Let's construct: The phenyl ring (call ring B) has at para position the side chain: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. Also the ring B has an NH (aniline) at the position where sulfonamide will attach (the nitrogen). So the SMILES for intermediate A: "Nc1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1". That's an aniline (NH attached to ring) with side chain. Yes.

Check: "Nc1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1". That matches.

Now we need to ensure that amide coupling step from 4-aminocinnamic acid and p-phenylenediamine yields that intermediate. Reaction: p-phenylenediamine has two NH2 groups; one reacts with acid to form amide, leaving the other free (the one attached to ring). The product SMILES would be "Nc1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1". Good.

Now we need reaction node for amide formation with template 401931, children: 4-aminocinnamic acid and p-phenylenediamine.

Thus intermediate A node will have child reaction.

Construct JSON accordingly.

Now final answer.
